<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

"Stand up the docker substrate for fs3: a BUILD container (pinned rust toolchain, persistent cargo caches in named volumes) and a RUN container (slim, binary mapped in) so a source change reaches the running daemon without any image rebuild and without restarting Postgres. Extend s001's db-only docker-compose.yml with a daemon service, prove the loop with a throwaway /health daemon, and pave the whole surface as a docker harness extension (verbs may shell through to script files) so agents never improvise engine commands. Engine-agnostic throughout: OrbStack today, podman by construction - compose-spec only, engine binary configurable. The build container is designed for later CI reuse (cross-platform matrix) but CI is not wired here."

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Fast dev loop: source change -> new binary running in the daemon container with zero image rebuilds; only the daemon service restarts, Postgres stays up.
- Build+run container pair: builds happen INSIDE a build container (pinned toolchain, cargo registry+target caches on named volumes); the run container maps the binary in.
- Engine-agnostic: works on OrbStack now and podman by construction - compose-spec-valid file, configurable engine binary, no Docker-exclusive features.
- Linux binaries from the mac host via the build container (native arm64, no emulation).
- Paved docker surface: a harness extension with stack up/down/status, build, daemon restart, logs, exec, and one-shot run-in-build-container - implementation may shell through to script files.
- Compose stack complete from day one: pgvector Postgres (already landed by s001) plus the daemon service this plan adds.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Real daemon functionality: the /health daemon is a throwaway POC - no config loading, no endpoints beyond /health; a later plan replaces it with the real fs3-daemon service surface.
- CI wiring: the build container is designed for CI cross-platform reuse (pinned toolchain, no host assumptions) but no CI pipeline is created here.
- PG schema/store design - deferred to the store plan; this plan only proves the pgvector container serves the extension.
- Zero-restart binary swap: a plain per-service container restart is the accepted reload (Jordan 2026-08-26).
- Host-side cross-compilation (cargo zigbuild): rejected in favour of building inside the build container (Jordan 2026-08-26).
- Live podman verification: podman compatibility is by construction (compose-spec + engine var); live verification waits until a podman host exists (open question).

<a id="implementation-summary"></a>

## Implementation Summary

"Two phases. Phase 1 (runs NOW, parallel to s001): prove everything as a POC under the plan's assets - build container with named-volume cargo caches, throwaway /health daemon, POC compose, reload loop, engine lint, results writeup. Phase 2 (GATED on s001 phase exit + o-prime fence coordination): extend the root docker-compose.yml with the daemon service, add docker/ Dockerfiles + scripts, wire the real fs3-daemon binary, land the docker harness extension (verbs shell through to the scripts) + docs/how/docker.md, and prove in-container test runs."

| Critical | s001 already landed a db-only docker-compose.yml (pgvector:pg16, port 5433, named volume, healthcheck) whose header defers the daemon service to a later plan. | Phase 2 EXTENDS this file - never replaces it; db service definition stays untouched. |
| Critical | Cargo caches (registry + target) must live on NAMED VOLUMES, not mac bind mounts - VirtioFS/osxfs overhead destroys incremental build times; source bind-mount read-only is fine. | tk-0101 mounts source ro + two named cache volumes; timing proof in done_when. |

| High | podman compatibility means compose-spec discipline: no docker-exclusive features (e.g. develop/watch, docker-specific extensions); engine binary must be configurable. | All scripts honour FS3_ENGINE (default docker); tk-0105 lints for violations; compose validated with `compose config`. |
| Medium | Jordan ruled the harness extension may shell through to plain script files - the harness verb is the discoverable surface, scripts are the implementation. | docker/scripts/* are the single implementation; the extension and humans call the same scripts. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Engine-agnostic always: every script honours FS3_ENGINE (default docker); no Docker-exclusive compose features; compose-spec-valid file.
- Never rebuild an image for a source change; never restart the db service in the reload loop.
- POC daemon is throwaway: /health only, no config, no gold-plating; phase 2 wires the real fs3-daemon binary.
- Phase 1 writes ONLY under docs/plans/002-docker-daemon-base/assets/poc/**; root compose, docker/, and .harness/extensions/** are phase-2 paths gated on s001 phase exit.
- Workshop 001 (plan 001) architecture rules still bind: exactly two ports, no new crates, daemon-side deps in fs3-daemon only.
- Never hand-edit any .dd.md (ddocs is the writer) or the-flow files (CLI-only).
- Shared volumes between build script and compose use explicit fixed names (`name:`/`external: true`) - compose project-name prefixing otherwise silently splits them; the paved down never deletes cache volumes.
